findings: Heidenheim amidah_qedushah.xml:34-50: the reusable Kedushah's j:conditional and j:endConditional are siblings inside the canonical div. They follow the Birnbaum amidah_qedushah.xml:36-75 pattern. This meets the ODD rules on xml:id, a following endConditional and a fully contained scope.

The caption 'קדושה לש״ץ בחזרת התפלה.' is a tei:note type=description, placed first after the conditional (line 48). It says both what the passage is and when it is said, so under 'Kinds of rubric' it is a description, not the conditional's instruction. The ODD rule allowing only instruction notes inside j:conditional is met. The conditional has no @type, so when the condition is undefined this opening description sets the scope off.

Every prayer word, every prayer-part milestone and the bare closing prayer-part terminator (line 49) sit inside that scope. The div corresp urn:x-opensiddur:text:prayer:amidah/qedushah and all part URNs are unchanged. Only the hael_haqadosh seal is present; no unprinted hamelekh_haqadosh variant was added.

Expanded index.xml:91-311: the preparatory Minchah gate has no instruction note and no @type, which is correct for a running-order gate. Each feature the gate fixes (service-time minha, the shabbat, yom-tov and aseret-ymei-tshuva aggregates, hebrew-date month/day) is declared again locally (122-162), as 'Conditions on a running order' requires. The declaration also sets the other service-time features to false. declare/endDeclare (122/309) and conditional/endConditional (91/311) are each sibling pairs.

Repetition (221-290): the instruction 'במניין: / With a minyan:' is the conditional's own tei:note type=instruction. The local declare sets recitation silent=false, repetition=true and quorum minyan=true, and its endDeclare (287) is a sibling.

No instruction or description note in either file has a rend attribute (index 166, 223, 293, 358 and the Modim descriptions 270-280 checked). The bare targets urn:x-opensiddur:text:prayer:amidah/qedushah (253) and the other Amidah targets carry no @project and are unchanged.
Cosmetic only: the xml:ids still say section_weekday_minchah* although the section is now Erev Rosh ha-Shanah Minchah. This has no effect on behaviour.

The reusable Kedushah requires both conditions: j:all of recitation/repetition=true and quorum/minyan=true. The evidence agrees: unit cases TT=1, FT=0, TF=0. By the all truth table, a false on either side settles the result as false.

The repetition gate still depends on the minyan: the outer condition is minyan=true, and the local declare then fixes repetition=true, silent=false and minyan=true. That decides the inner Kedushah guard even with no date or quorum given. Evidence: 'undated' inner_qedushah_guard_resolved=true, with the outer alternatives kept.

The silent Amidah declares repetition=false and transcludes qedushat_hashem, so Kedushah cannot appear twice. Evidence: erev-alone gives Minchah included, Kedushah 0; erev-with-minyan gives Kedushah 1.

The Minchah gate is Elul 29 in the Nisan-first numbering: month 6, day 29. JLPTEI-3.md:1077 defines month 1 as Nisan, and compute.py gets Hebrew dates from pyluach, which also starts at Nisan. The gate closes at line 311, before section_morning (313). Evidence: Elul 28, 3 Tishrei and 1 Tishrei all exclude Minchah and give Kedushah 0.

The gate tests shabbat=false, which is always true on 29 Elul (Rosh Hashanah never falls on Sunday), and yom-tov/aseret-ymei-tshuva=false, which are also always true on that date. These are redundant but harmless, and they correctly mark the ordinary-season context.

limits: Read-only static review. I did not run Schematron/RelaxNG validation, the features.yaml registry check, validate_urn_references, or the compiler. Compiler behaviour comes only from the summary JSON, which records no command, settings file, location, commit or output excerpt.
I did not trace the derivation code in compute.py; only its header was read. The month numbering rests on the schema text and pyluach's convention.

The spec says a Hebrew date declared after a secular one re-derives the secular date as 'the evening before, at a time after nightfall' (JLPTEI-3.md:1104-1106). The local month/day declaration could therefore move a dated 15:00 context to after nightfall. That is harmless here, because service-time and the aggregates are declared explicitly in the same block and the erev-with-minyan case shows the expected output. But that rests on the evidence, not on tracing the code.

The Heidenheim Kedushah prints only the haEl seal, as agreed. If it is ever transcluded in a Ten Days context outside this gated Minchah, it would set haEl without a haMelekh alternative. None of the cases covers that.
When the Kedushah condition is false, the canonical div with its corresp remains as an empty shell. This matches the Birnbaum pattern and is not counted as a defect.
